To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
trust is the most important factor for successful e-commerce.
trust is a complex construct that can be influenced by a large number of variables.

the user interface should: • be easy and intuitive to use; • be trustworthy, i.e. not appear to be a scam; • be perceived as secure, i.e. no personal information should be compromised; • be perceived to be reliable, i.e. it should be possible to get a response from a human; • be perceived not to be a risk; and • be perceived to offer good value for money.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of the user interface to support the user experience and to maximise perceived trustworthiness.
the affective design of e-commerce user interfaces.
the design of user interfaces that are able to increase perceived trustworthiness and acceptance of an e-commerce system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trust is an important factor for the success of e-commerce, and that the user interface design of e-commerce sites can have a significant impact on the perceived trustworthiness.
trust is not a single, isolated issue, but rather the result of a complex set of interrelated factors.
the design of the user interface is not the only issue to consider when trying to maximize perceived trustworthiness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trust is a key element of e-commerce user experience.

trust in an e- commerce system is not only a result of the user experience design but also the result of the trustworthiness of the e-commerce provider, the e-commerce provider’s business model, and the user’s personal trust in the Internet and e-commerce in general.
the design of the user interface should be consistent, clear, easy-to-use and easy-to-navigate, with the user interface design being consistent with the overall look and feel of the site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
user interface designers need to be aware of the fact that trust in an e-Commerce system is based on a complex set of factors, some of which are beyond their control.
the user interface design should be seen in a broader context and not in isolation from other factors.
the user experience design process needs to be extended to include a number of factors that go beyond the mere user interface.
